solution: A move sends each chosen animal to a neighbouring enclosure whose animal also moves, so it is a permutation whose cycles are vertex-disjoint simple cycles of the graph, and the ban on reusing a tunnel forbids 2-cycles; the reachable arrangements are therefore the orbit of the group generated by rotations of simple cycles of length at least 3. Every cycle lies inside one bridgeless component, so animals never cross a bridge and each 2-edge-connected component is decided independently, a singleton having to already hold its target. A component that is exactly one cycle of length L admits only its L rotations, checked in linear time by searching the target sequence inside the doubled initial sequence (n is 4e5, so the naive O(L^2) rotation scan is too slow). Any other 2-edge-connected component generates A_N, and S_N as soon as it contains an even cycle, which happens exactly when some block is not an odd cycle (a 2-connected non-cycle graph contains a theta subgraph, whose three cycles cannot all be odd); so multiset equality suffices unless every block is an odd cycle and all types in the component are distinct, in which case the induced permutation must also be even, a repeated type supplying an odd stabiliser element that removes the parity obstruction. Bridges, 2-edge-connected components and blocks all come out of one Tarjan low-link pass, so the whole check is O(n + m).
statement_summary: Each of up to 400000 enclosures holds one animal type and has a desired final type, the targets being a permutation of the initial types, and tunnels join some pairs of enclosures. One move simultaneously shifts a chosen set of animals to adjacent enclosures so that the moved animals permute among themselves, with no tunnel reused, which forbids swapping two neighbours. Decide whether repeated moves can reach the desired arrangement.
notes: Verified by brute force: verify_zoomanagement.py BFSes the true reachable colourings under vertex-disjoint simple-cycle rotations and compares against the rule on every connected graph on 3, 4 and 5 vertices (770 graphs) plus 120 random 6-vertex graphs, with distinct, two-colour and duplicated palettes, and on targeted 7/8-vertex structures (triangle chains and hubs, C5+C3, theta graphs, odd-cycle-plus-bridge, disconnected) - 0 mismatches, and all four samples match. A separate run confirms the generated group directly: single cycle -> Z_L, 2-edge-connected non-cycle with an even cycle -> S_N, all blocks odd cycles -> exactly A_N (checked at N=7 for three different odd cacti and at N=9 for two C5s sharing a vertex, |G| = N!/2). VOCABULARY GAP: the real content is permutation-group theory - the group generated by cycle rotations is A_N or S_N - and the taxonomy has no group-theory / permutation-group label; parity-argument is the closest carrier for the even-permutation test. articulation-points stands in for biconnected-component (block) decomposition, which is what the odd-cycle test needs; tarjan would fit as well. bridge-tree is listed at low confidence because the solution needs the bridge tree's nodes (the 2-edge-connected components) but never its tree structure. string-matching covers the rotation-equivalence test (search e in b+b); KMP, Z-function or hashing all work, so the family label is used rather than a specific one. union-find (grouping non-bridge edges) and dfs are scaffolding and are deliberately not labelled. Not judge-verified - no submission was made.
